subject: Addenda scoping: combined GLBA + FERPA requests (MicroBank & Meadowfield Academy)
messages:
From: procurement@microbank.com
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: tim.arnold@microbank.com
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFQ: combined GLBA & FERPA addenda feasibility

Hi Lukas,

We are evaluating Redwood for two separate programs: MicroBank (consumer banking) and Meadowfield Academy (K-12 district partner). Both have distinct regulatory requirements — MicroBank needs GLBA-compliant processing with US data residency and strict subprocessor restrictions; Meadowfield requires FERPA protections and a signed BAA for certain student health records that may flow through some of our integrations.

Before we open a formal procurement track, can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide separate DPA/addenda language for GLBA and FERPA (we may need a combined/dual addendum document)
- Offer evidence (SOC 2 Type II, encryption attestations, KMS keying approach) and a current subprocessors list
- Support US-only residency for both accounts (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private options)

Attached is our high-level RFP packet and a short table of data flows. Please confirm a rough timeline for evidence and whether you recommend a pilot setup (POC) vs. direct deployment.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
MicroBank
(attachment: MicroBank_RFP_attachments.pdf)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: procurement@microbank.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFQ: combined GLBA & FERPA addenda feasibility

Hi — thanks for the clear summary and the RFP packet. Looping in Monica (security), Vanessa (legal) and Marissa (account lead) so we can coordinate.

Quick answers up front:
- We can produce tailored addenda for GLBA and FERPA; in practice our legal team produces a DPA with modular addenda clauses so we can either combine or keep them separate depending on contract needs.
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and an encryption attestation; for key control we offer customer-managed KMS options on Dedicated/Private, and Redwood-managed KMS for Hosted with strict access controls.
- US-only residency is achievable in Dedicated or Private deployments; Hosted can be restricted to US regions but is a multi-tenant service and may not satisfy all GLBA procurement controls.

Can you confirm: data types (PII, financial account numbers, student records), expected steady-state token/embedding volumes, whether MicroBank requires physical isolation (on-prem or dedicated GPU pools), and whether Meadowfield will require a BAA (we can draft one but need to confirm scope)?

Propose a 30-minute scoping call tomorrow (Thu) or Monday to align on these points.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFQ: combined GLBA & FERPA addenda feasibility — security checklist

Folks —

I reviewed the RFP and sketched the evidence checklist below. If MicroBank and Meadowfield confirm the flows, we can provide items 1–6 within the timelines noted.

Minimum items we need from them:
- Confirmation of data categories (PII / account numbers / student education records / student health data)
- Expected retention windows and deletion triggers

What Redwood will provide (subject to NDA where applicable):
1) SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) — available within 2 business days after countersigning an NDA/LOU.
2) Subprocessor inventory (current) — attached as CSV; we will mark EU/other-region subprocessors.
3) Encryption at rest/in transit attestation; description of KMS options and ability to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) on Dedicated/Private.
4) Architecture notes on isolation: Dedicated GPU pools per customer and Private VPC/on-prem options; suggested configuration for GLBA workloads (dedicated pool + VPC peering).
5) Audit logs and retention policy; we can provide log export options for compliance teams.
6) Draft addenda language: GLBA module, FERPA module, and BAA template (for student health records).

For GLBA we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private for the highest assurance — Hosted can be considered for lower-risk functions after legal sign-off. For FERPA, BAA is typically required only when health data is involved; for standard education records we use a FERPA addendum and data minimization controls.

Attaching current subprocessor inventory: subprocessor_inventory_v3.csv (contains service, region, purpose).

Monica Patel
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(attachment: subprocessor_inventory_v3.csv)

From: procurement@microbank.com
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: tim.arnold@microbank.com, legal@meadowfield.edu
Date: 2027-05-22T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFQ: combined GLBA & FERPA addenda feasibility — clarifications

Lukas / team —

Thanks for the rapid response. A few clarifications from MicroBank and Meadowfield after internal review:
- MicroBank will require full US-only processing for GLBA-covered data and prefers Dedicated with dedicated GPU pools; physical isolation is a plus but not mandatory if contractual isolation and audit capabilities are present.
- Meadowfield indicates they will require a signed BAA due to student health integrations (school nurse app). They are OK with a Dedicated deployment scoped to their account.
- Both parties request an explicit subprocessors list and a redlineable addenda draft for review by their counsel.
- Please provide an estimated timeline for: delivery of SOC2 redact, subprocessor inventory confirmation, and a first draft of the GLBA + FERPA addenda.

Proposed PoC plan: 4-week security/ops POC with exportable audit logs and weekly checkpoints. Can Redwood commit to that cadence?

We will also need a cost ballpark for Dedicated (monthly) and an estimate for Private (one-time + monthly ops).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call. DocuSign request pending: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC-1458

Procurement Team
MicroBank

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: procurement@microbank.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFQ: combined GLBA & FERPA addenda feasibility — next steps

Team — great, this is actionable. Proposed next steps and commitments from Redwood:

1) Evidence delivery
- SOC 2 Type II (redacted): we will provide within 2 business days after NDA countersign.
- Confirmed subprocessor inventory: we will mark US-only processing capabilities and note which subprocessors have EU routing; target delivery: 1 business day after request.
- Encryption/KMS attestation and BYOK guidance: 2 business days.

2) Addenda and legal materials
- Draft GLBA module and FERPA module + BAA template: first draft to be shared within 3 business days for redline. Vanessa will lead legal drafting.

3) Technical path for compliance
- Recommended path for MicroBank: Dedicated reserved capacity with customer VPC peering and optional BYOK; we will supply architecture notes and a configuration checklist for audit.
- Meadowfield: Dedicated scoped to the school district; BAA to be included for the nurse/health workflows.

4) PoC and pricing
- PoC cadence: 4-week security/ops POC with weekly checkpoints — Redwood commits to providing audit exports and a named security contact.
- Ballpark pricing: Dedicated starting at $Xk/month (final depends on reserved GPUs and throughput); Private/on-prem estimate requires sizing call. Marissa will follow up with a formal quote.

Action items: Vanessa to produce drafts; Monica to prepare evidence bundle; Marissa to scope pricing and propose PO/contract path. Can we schedule an internal/legal <-> MicroBank call tomorrow 10:00 AM PT?

Regards,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
